metadata.title: SSPP Template – Trusted Cloud
metadata.remarks: Normative SSPP template defining institutional trust expectations for third-party cloud platforms (primarily SaaS). Addresses platform-level security, isolation, governance, and assurance without duplicating application, identity, or regulatory controls.

import-profile.remarks: Imports institutional baseline security and governance requirements applicable to cloud platforms.

system-characteristics.system-description: Baseline trust and governance expectations for cloud service providers hosting institutional workloads or data, independent of business function or application logic.

props.name: institutional-owner
props.remarks: Defines cloud trust posture, assurance expectations, and institutional risk tolerance.

props.name: business-owner
props.remarks: Owns the business relationship with the cloud provider and accepts residual platform risk.

props.name: cloud-service-model
props.remarks: This SSPP template is primarily scoped to Software-as-a-Service platforms.

props.name: governance-model
props.remarks: Cloud trust expectations are centrally defined and assessed; individual services inherit this baseline.

props.name: shared-responsibility-model
props.remarks: The provider is responsible for underlying platform security; the institution is responsible for access, configuration, and data use within the service.

props.name: tenant-isolation
props.remarks: Logical isolation between tenants MUST be enforced by the provider.

props.name: data-residency-transparency
props.remarks: The provider MUST disclose regions used for primary data storage, backups, and disaster recovery.

props.name: provider-admin-access
props.remarks: Provider privileged access to customer tenants MUST be controlled, limited, and auditable.

props.name: security-assurance
props.remarks: The provider SHOULD maintain independent security attestations (e.g., SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001).

props.name: logging-and-evidence
props.remarks: The platform MUST provide sufficient logs or evidence to support investigations and audits.

props.name: incident-notification
props.remarks: The provider MUST notify customers of security incidents affecting customer data or service availability.

props.name: subprocessor-governance
props.remarks: Use of subprocessors MUST be disclosed, with change notification and security obligation flow-down.

props.name: data-exit-and-decommissioning
props.remarks: The provider MUST support data export and commit contractually to data deletion upon termination.

props.name: compliance-evidence-availability
props.remarks: The provider MUST make compliance reports and audit evidence available to customers under NDA.

props.name: regulatory-support
props.remarks: The provider SHOULD support customer compliance with relevant regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR) through contractual commitments and evidence.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Referenced for cloud security principles and shared responsibility models, including loss of direct control, provider-consumer responsibility boundaries across IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS, and the role of governance and visibility as compensating trust mechanisms.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Referenced for cyber resiliency guidance identifying cloud services as critical enabling dependencies and establishing expectations for survivability, controlled degradation, and recovery across provider and service disruptions.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Referenced for formal definitions of cloud computing, service models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS), and deployment models. Trusted Cloud patterns and SSPP assertions rely on these definitions to establish responsibility boundaries and trust assumptions.

system-implementation.remarks: This SSPP template defines platform trust expectations only. Provider-specific implementations are documented in SSPP instances derived from this template.

components.title: Cloud Platform Service
components.description: Third-party cloud platform providing hosting, processing, or management of institutional workloads.

components.title: Cloud Assurance and Evidence
components.description: Provider security attestations, audit reports, and compliance evidence available for institutional review.

roles.title: Cloud Security Policy Authority
roles.remarks: Defines institutional cloud trust posture, minimum assurance expectations, and acceptable risk.

props.name: nice-work-role
props.remarks: Executive Cyber Leadership per NIST NICE Framework (SP 800-181).

roles.title: Cloud Architecture Authority
roles.remarks: Ensures cloud platforms align with institutional architecture, trust models, and dependency constraints.

props.name: nice-work-role
props.remarks: Security Architect per NIST NICE Framework.

roles.title: Cloud Security Assessor
roles.remarks: Performs platform trust assessments, reviews provider evidence, and produces SARs and risk recommendations.

props.name: nice-work-role
props.remarks: Risk Management Specialist per NIST NICE Framework.

control-implementation.remarks: Control satisfaction is demonstrated through provider disclosures, independent attestations, contractual commitments, and evidence availability rather than customer-managed technical controls.
